arguments.subject: Delgado Housing Case Strategy Conference - meeting summary
arguments.body:
Minutes of the Delgado Housing Case Strategy Conference meeting (2026-04-29):

Amara Singh: Morning everyone — thanks for being on time. I want to keep us tight today, we've got four things to get through and I'd like to wrap by 11. Kofi, Rosa, you good to dive in?
Kofi Mensah: Morning. Yep, ready.
Rosa Delgado: Hi Amara, hi Kofi. Ready.
Amara Singh: Great. Agenda: habitability evidence, the answer and counterclaim, rent escrow, hearing timeline. Let's start with the evidence. Rosa, you've been keeping the records — can you walk us through what we have?
Rosa Delgado: So I have three main things. First is the unit 4B repair log I started in November — 23 entries now, the heat going out, the leak in the bathroom ceiling, the mold behind the tub. Second is the building management text messages, about 41 of them, and most of their replies are either nothing or 'we'll send someone.' Third is the Harbor County Code Enforcement inspection from April 9 — the inspector cited three violations, the heat, the leak, and the mold. I also have a lot of photos but the older ones don't have dates on them, and my neighbor in 4C said she might write a statement but she hasn't committed.
Kofi Mensah: Yeah, I'd lead with the log, the texts, and the code enforcement report. The photos are fine as supporting material but without dates they won't carry much, and I wouldn't count on the neighbor statement.
Amara Singh: Agreed. So the repair log, the texts, and the code enforcement report are our core exhibits, and the photos go in as supporting?
Rosa Delgado: Yes, that makes sense to me.
Kofi Mensah: Plus one.
Amara Singh: Good. Decision: repair log, building management texts, and the code enforcement report are the core exhibits. Kofi, can you compile them into an exhibit set this week so I can review by Monday?
Kofi Mensah: Will do. I'll have it in the case file by end of day Friday.
Amara Singh: Perfect. Item two — the answer and counterclaim against Maplewood Properties LLC. I want to land on the scope today. Kofi, what's your read?
Kofi Mensah: I've been going back and forth. If we only answer and deny the nonpayment claim, we're just playing defense. I'd file the answer with a habitability counterclaim asking for rent abatement going back to November, when the heat first failed. That's a strong enough period to matter, and the log and the inspection back it up.
Rosa Delgado: I agree with that. And on the dates — the heat first went out November 3, the ceiling leak started in early January, and the mold showed up after that. I wrote each one down the day it happened, so the log lines up.
Amara Singh: That works for me. Any concern about claiming back to November when the texts to building management only start in December?
Kofi Mensah: Some, but the November 3 log entry notes she called the office that day. I think it's worth claiming the full period and letting the landlord argue it down.
Amara Singh: Okay. Decision: we file the answer with a habitability counterclaim against Maplewood Properties LLC seeking abatement from November. I'll draft it, and we file by May 6. Kofi, you'll get Rosa's signed verification once the draft is ready?
Kofi Mensah: Yep.
Amara Singh: Good. Item three — rent escrow. Daniel confirmed the $4,200 figure last week. Rosa, how do you want to handle the deposit?
Rosa Delgado: I've been setting the rent aside since February like you told me, so I have it. I can get a money order from my credit union on Friday morning for the full $4,200 and bring it to the Harbor County Housing Court clerk the same day. Then I'll bring the receipt and a copy of the money order to the clinic so it's in the file.
Kofi Mensah: That works. I'd just flag that the $4,200 assumes the court doesn't ask for May's rent to be added before the hearing — if it does, that number goes up.
Amara Singh: Noted. We can revisit if the clerk raises it. Decision: $4,200 deposited in escrow with Harbor County Housing Court, Rosa brings the money order proof to the clinic. Kofi, please track the deposit in the case file today.
Kofi Mensah: On it.
Amara Singh: Last item — hearing timeline. I want to be thoughtful here, because Maplewood's counsel floated the Tenant Mediation Program. If we agree too quickly we lose leverage, and if we refuse outright the court may see us as unreasonable. Where do we land?
Rosa Delgado: My preference is to keep the May 14 hearing. They've promised me repairs three times since November and nothing happened. If they actually start fixing things, then I'd be willing to talk in mediation.
Kofi Mensah: I like that. Mediation hasn't gone well with this landlord on the last two cases we had against them.
Amara Singh: Agreed. Decision: we proceed to the May 14 hearing and decline the Tenant Mediation Program unless repairs actually begin. Rosa, you'll tell Kofi right away if any repair crew shows up?
Rosa Delgado: Yes.
Amara Singh: And Kofi, you'll coordinate with Hannah on docketing the filing deadline and the hearing date, since she's lining up the filing packet?
Kofi Mensah: Yep, I'll loop Hannah in this week.
Amara Singh: Perfect. Quick sanity check on action items — Rosa: money order and escrow deposit Friday, proof to the clinic, tell Kofi about any repairs. Kofi: exhibit set by Friday, escrow tracking today, signed verification, docketing with Hannah. Me: I'll draft the answer and counterclaim for filing by May 6 and update Daniel on the plan. Anything I'm missing?
Rosa Delgado: I think that covers it.
Kofi Mensah: One thing — do we want to set a formal check-in cadence between now and May 14? I'd suggest weekly given how much we have to land before the hearing.
Amara Singh: Good call. Same time next Wednesday, and I'll keep this slot held through May 13.
Kofi Mensah: Works.
Rosa Delgado: Works.
Amara Singh: One more thing while I have you both — on scope, are we still aligned that this case is the nonpayment defense and the habitability counterclaim, and that a separate repair action or a retaliation claim waits until after the hearing? I don't want us to take on more than we can prove by May 14.
Rosa Delgado: Understood. Just the defense and counterclaim for now. If things get worse after the hearing we can talk about the rest then.
Kofi Mensah: Same.
Amara Singh: Great. And on what we keep building before the hearing — updated dated photos of the ceiling and the tub, and a request for a code enforcement re-inspection. Anything else you think we should capture?
Rosa Delgado: I could keep a daily temperature log with the thermometer Kofi gave me — just the morning and evening reading, every day until the hearing.
Kofi Mensah: Plus one on that. Easy to do, and judges like it.
Amara Singh: Added. So ongoing evidence: dated photos, re-inspection request, daily temperature log. Rosa, please start the temperature log tonight and bring it to next Wednesday's check-in.
Rosa Delgado: Will do.
Amara Singh: Okay — anything else for either of you before I let you go?
Kofi Mensah: Nothing from me.
Rosa Delgado: Nothing here.
Amara Singh: Okay, I think that's everything on my list — let's wrap here. Thanks everyone for staying focused.
Kofi Mensah: Thanks Amara — good session.
Rosa Delgado: Yes, thank you both. Talk soon!
Amara Singh: Alright, I've got to jump to my 11 — talk soon.

Kofi Mensah: Heads up if you're coming in Friday — the elevator at the clinic is out again. They say it'll be fixed by next week, but I wouldn't count on it.
Rosa Delgado: That's okay, it's only the second floor. I'm used to stairs with our building anyway.
Kofi Mensah: Friday walk-in hours are nine to noon. If you come for the drop-off, just tell the front desk you're there to see me.
Rosa Delgado: I'll come early. Last time I came on a Friday the line was out the door by ten.
Kofi Mensah: Good idea. And parking out front is a mess right now — they tore up the lot on the side for repaving, so it's all meters on the street.
Rosa Delgado: I'll take the bus then. The 14 stops right on the corner after the credit union.
Kofi Mensah: That's probably easier. I circled for fifteen minutes on Monday before I found a spot.
